title: What Happens If You Invest $5 a Day?

blocks.text: I invested five dollars every single day.
blocks.visual: Insert, close-up on a hand folding a $5 bill and sliding it into a clear jar labeled "SAVINGS"

blocks.text: First deposit, same ritual, five dollars into the jar every morning before work.
blocks.visual: Insert, tight shot of a wristwatch at 7:10 and a hand dropping a $5 bill into the jar

blocks.text: Two weeks later the jar looks the same, but the account linked to it started compounding.
blocks.visual: Medium, animated bank app screen showing a deposit labeled "$5" and a tiny interest number appearing

blocks.text: I used a hypothetical example, imagine a 7 percent annual return to see how small adds up.
blocks.visual: Wide, simple animated farm field where seedlings sprout each day along a row labeled "5$"

blocks.text: Analogy, it's like planting seeds every day, then letting rain and sun do the heavy lifting over decades.
blocks.visual: Insert, close-up of a single seed in soil, then a split showing small sprout and a taller plant labeled "interest"

blocks.text: Concrete numbers as an example only: $5 a day equals $1,825 a year invested at 7 percent compound annually.
blocks.visual: Medium, calculator display reading "1825" then an arrow to a small chart labeled "7%"

blocks.text: After 20 years that example grows to about $75,000, again this is a hypothetical 7 percent scenario.
blocks.visual: Wide, animated bar that rises to a label "Year 20: $75,000" next to a smaller bar labeled "Contributions"

blocks.text: At year 30 that same example reaches roughly $172,000, mostly driven by interest compounding on prior gains.
blocks.visual: Insert, animated line chart showing a curve accelerating then a highlight at "Year 30: $172,400"

blocks.text: Stretch to 40 years in this same example and you get about $364,000, demonstrating how time multiplies results.
blocks.visual: Wide, stacked bars for Year 20, Year 30, Year 40 rising left to right with labels and values

blocks.text: Important note, this uses one example rate. Real returns vary, fees matter, and results are not guaranteed.
blocks.visual: Medium, close-up on a document titled "Example Only" with a finger tapping the words "Not guaranteed"

blocks.text: So the real takeaway, small daily amounts plus time and reinvestment can build significant sums, depending on returns.
blocks.visual: Wide, montage of jar filling, bank app balance rising, and a calendar flipping years quickly

blocks.text: Would you start $5 a day or wait for a bigger lump sum?
blocks.visual: Close_up, two labeled envelopes on a table, one titled "$5/day" and the other "Lump Sum", hand hovering between them
